counterfactual_missing_items: evidence of spinal cord compression on MRI
decisive_items: developed lower back pain and a tingling sensation radiating along the posterior aspect of her bilateral lower extremities
0/5 strength of the bilateral lower extremities (MRC scale)
Abnormal T2 cord signal from T8 to T9 disc level downwards to the conus medullaris
response.rationale: R2 is the most complete, integrating acute clinical presentation (pain, tingling, weakness) with MRI findings, and has no contradictions. R3 only cites the MRI finding, lacking the clinical syndrome. R5 also cites the MRI but is contradicted by negative CSF, which argues against an inflammatory cause.

rejected.why: Only provides the MRI finding without the clinical presentation; does not explain the acute onset and weakness, and the imaging does not show compression.
The negative CSF analysis directly contradicts an inflammatory etiology such as transverse myelitis, and the clinical picture is more consistent with a non-inflammatory spinal cord injury.
